newsitem.title: GERMANY: Britain's Prince Andrew in German bomb hoax.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Prince Andrew in German bomb hoax.

text.p: Britain's Prince Andrew cancelled a book-signing ceremony at Duesseldorf's city hall on Wednesday after authorities received an anonymous bomb threat, police said. No bomb was found.
"It was a bad joke and there was no political motivation," a police spokesman said. No bomb was found in a police search.
Queen Elizabeth's second son, taking part in festivities marking the 50th anniversary of the founding of North Rhine-Westphalia, had planned to sign his name in the city of Duesseldorf's Golden Book.
The British military helped set up the post-war state government of North Rhine-Westphalia in 1946.
Andrew did sign the Golden Book later on Wednesday after police brought the book to the prince at the British consulate.
The incident came less than three days after British security forces destroyed a suspected bomb in a car abandoned in central Belfast by maverick Irish republican guerrillas.
The Irish Republican Army, fighting to oust Britain from Northern Ireland, called off its truce in February.
